# Station

> Type-safe background jobs, schedules, Station Networks, beacons, DAG workflows, browser-local execution, persistent sandbox workspaces and agent-controlled browser sessions for TypeScript.

Station 3.0.0 is a modular TypeScript framework. Station 3.0 separates station-daemon (headless runners/API, stationd), station-runtime-cli (station command), station-client (transport), and station-dashboard (independent UI). station-kit is retired without compatibility exports. Start the daemon with stationd; start station-dashboard separately with STATION_DAEMON_URL, PORT and STATION_DASHBOARD_HOST. Clients can connect to remote daemons and closing them does not stop work. station-images packages independently compiled native or bundled JavaScript signals, broadcast planners and beacons under station.process/v1. Operator-admin registries support publish/install/run, granted environment values, compatible Headquarters catalog synchronization and immutable worker pins. Registry metadata and blobs use separate pluggable adapters with shared validation; file/memory implementations are included. Custom registry.storage backends use verified local execution caches and keep provider credentials in the daemon; PostgreSQL/S3 registry drivers are not bundled. Docker image execution requires reviewed runtime policy and an independent station-image-reaper; tenant-scoped registry grants and a fixed dedicated-worker execution gateway are implemented with real Docker fixture coverage. Enrollment admission/revocation, reconnectable bounded-replay TUI streams, mixed native planner grants, scoped invocation artifact brokering, audited environment overrides and explicit beacon rollout have executable acceptance coverage. Invocation media uses operator-granted local storage without automatic cross-worker transfer or a general media HTTP API. Intended Linux production-host validation was explicitly deferred. The 20-package release dry run and isolated packed installs passed; npm publish permissions remain unverified. Check the acceptance map for the exact tested boundaries. The full deployment platform remains incomplete. For browser-local work, use the experimental station-browser runtime with explicit registries and IndexedDB; it has been available since Station 2.3.0. Browser workers use cooperative execution and cannot guarantee continuous work after a PWA closes. In the Node runtime, signals are isolated background jobs, broadcasts are DAG workflows, beacons are supervised long-running processes, schedules provide interval and timezone-aware cron execution, and Station Networks coordinate work across a Headquarters and worker stations. The experimental station-sandbox and station-browser-use packages add separate persistent workspaces and agent-controlled browser sessions, routed to their owning workers through Headquarters. Host adapters are for trusted workloads. Public tenants require scoped keys, dedicated private workers, container backends and independently enforced network/storage controls. Browser agent tools provide workflow-scoped sessions, structured DOM/ARIA observations and native image results; the Foundry example demonstrates the model image bridge. Profiles, files and configured recordings can persist, but live processes are not restored. Local browser/protocol tests do not require a model key; the paid real-model test is opt-in. These are execution primitives, not a complete multi-tenant hosting platform. Node remains the default child runtime; Bun signal/beacon execution is opt-in through ProcessRuntime. Prefer the Markdown links below when supplying documentation to an agent.

## Start here

- [Getting started](https://station.dterminal.net/docs/getting-started.md): Install Station, define and run a signal, add persistence, and prepare a production configuration.
- [Docker Compose and persistent agents](https://station.dterminal.net/docs/docker-compose.md): Containerized Station controller and separate dashboard, sibling agent sandboxes, Docker socket boundaries, persistent volumes and engine failure recovery.
- [Browser runtime (experimental)](https://station.dterminal.net/docs/browser.md): Build signals, DAGs, and beacons in Web Workers or service workers with IndexedDB, explicit wake handling, recovery, and browser execution limits. Includes beacon configuration and start-mode behavior.
- [Sandboxes](https://station.dterminal.net/docs/sandboxes.md): Illustrated workspace lifecycle: host and container boundaries, commands versus terminals and services, custom tools and Git, internal networking, persistence and recovery.
- [Browser Use](https://station.dterminal.net/docs/browser-use.md): Illustrated agent browser loop, adapter choices, session/profile/checkpoint distinctions, scoped tools, screenshot playback, human control and lifecycle limitations.
- [Sandbox and Browser Use (experimental)](https://station.dterminal.net/docs/execution.md): Build persistent shell workspaces and agent-controlled browser sessions through Headquarters. Covers host/container adapters, tenant authorization, enforced network/storage controls, agent tools and image observations, dashboard subpages, recordings, recovery and optional Bun children.
- [Dashboard guide](https://station.dterminal.net/docs/dashboard.md): Operate the independent Station dashboard, inspect runs, and understand Headquarters fleet views.
- [Station Networks](https://station.dterminal.net/docs/network.md): Scale execution across Headquarters and worker stations with placement, capacity, leases, and draining.
- [Agent skill](https://station.dterminal.net/docs/agent-skill.md): Install and use the Station coding-agent skill and its bundled API references.

## Guides and operations

- [Station Images and registry](https://station.dterminal.net/docs/images.md): Publish native and bundled JavaScript exports with resumable uploads; stage generations, bind environment references, activate/rollback/drain, prepare cold workers, target private registries and configure tenant grants. Includes nested dashboard workflows, Docker reaping and a numbered acceptance map.
- [Remote triggers](https://station.dterminal.net/docs/remote-triggers.md): Trigger Station signals from another service through the authenticated HTTP API.
- [Dynamic broadcasts](https://station.dterminal.net/docs/dynamic-broadcasts.md): Create runtime-defined DAG workflows with expressions, validation, and versioned definitions.
- [Schedules](https://station.dterminal.net/docs/schedules.md): Configure interval and cron schedules with timezones, overlap policy, and misfire handling.
- [Environment variables](https://station.dterminal.net/docs/environment.md): Manage global and target-scoped runtime variables without exposing secret values.
- [Tauri desktop](https://station.dterminal.net/docs/tauri-desktop.md): Bundle Station as a local Tauri sidecar with provisioned authentication.

## API reference

- [Signals](https://station.dterminal.net/docs/signals.md): Signal builder, runner, queue adapter, lifecycle, concurrency, placement, and trigger APIs.
- [Broadcasts](https://station.dterminal.net/docs/broadcasts.md): Static and dynamic DAG workflows, execution policies, adapters, and subscribers.
- [Beacons](https://station.dterminal.net/docs/beacons.md): Supervised long-running processes, instances, restart policies, health, and service proxying.
- [Expressions](https://station.dterminal.net/docs/expressions.md): Deterministic expression AST, parser, evaluator, validation, and workflow references.
- [Adapters](https://station.dterminal.net/docs/adapters.md): Memory, SQLite, PostgreSQL, MySQL, and Redis persistence and coordination adapters.
- [Station Daemon](https://station.dterminal.net/docs/station.md): Headless daemon configuration, separate CLI/dashboard clients, authentication, REST API, runners, and deployment.

## Examples

- [Examples overview](https://station.dterminal.net/docs/examples.md): Index of complete examples arranged from first signal to distributed fleets.
- [Browser lab](https://station.dterminal.net/docs/examples/browser.md): Run the local browser prototype, interrupt and recover work, exercise all three primitives, and run real-browser checks.
- [Basic signal](https://station.dterminal.net/docs/examples/basic.md): Minimal signal definition and trigger.
- [Typed output](https://station.dterminal.net/docs/examples/with-output.md): Declare and consume validated signal output.
- [Signal steps](https://station.dterminal.net/docs/examples/with-steps.md): Checkpoint multi-step work and inspect step progress.
- [Recurring signal](https://station.dterminal.net/docs/examples/recurring.md): Run a signal on a simple recurring interval.
- [Retries](https://station.dterminal.net/docs/examples/with-retries.md): Retry failed work with bounded attempts and backoff.
- [SQLite persistence](https://station.dterminal.net/docs/examples/with-sqlite.md): Persist signal state locally with the SQLite adapter.
- [Broadcast workflow](https://station.dterminal.net/docs/examples/broadcast.md): Compose signals into a typed DAG workflow.
- [ETL pipeline](https://station.dterminal.net/docs/examples/etl-pipeline.md): Extract, transform, and load data as a multi-stage broadcast.
- [CI pipeline](https://station.dterminal.net/docs/examples/ci-pipeline.md): Model build, test, and deployment stages with workflow dependencies.
- [Fleet monitor](https://station.dterminal.net/docs/examples/fleet-monitor.md): Supervise a long-running process with beacon health and restart behavior.
- [Beacon service](https://station.dterminal.net/docs/examples/beacon.md): Define, configure, start, and stop a supervised beacon instance.
- [Station Network](https://station.dterminal.net/docs/examples/station-network.md): Run a Headquarters and two workers against shared SQLite coordination.

- [Detailed Sandbox guide](https://github.com/porkytheblack/station/blob/main/packages/station-sandbox/GUIDE.md): Custom tool installation, Git workflows, files, terminals, services, tenant RPCs and backend-specific recovery.
